character_facts: The armored leader calls Crow 'master' or is called 'master' by Crow, indicating a command hierarchy.
The leader believes triumph requires the death of those tied to an engineered betrayal.
Crow responds obediently to navigation or speed commands.
Metablade is dead, ruined, or reduced to remains by this point.
The group includes a baby traveling aboard the ship.

Crow, depicted as a floating blue brain-like entity
A baby or very young child

continuity_links: The page follows a battle or destructive act that has just ended with the eradication of Flos.
The mention of engineered treachery indicates an earlier plot involving deliberate manipulation.
The order to head for the Golden Planet sets up the next destination in the story.
dialogue_meaning: The narration emphasizes the sudden total destruction of a once-lush world.
The destruction kills the flowers and Zombras, but poisonous insects endure.
A surviving character pays respect to Metablade's remains.
The crew is urgently redirecting the ship toward the Golden Planet.
The baby burps after being encouraged by an attendant.
The leader treats the recent outcome as incomplete and wants to manipulate events so enemies strike the Empire.
Crow serves as a subordinate pilot or ship intelligence that obeys the order for maximum speed.

lore_facts: A planet called Flos is described as a garden planet.
Zombras inhabit or are associated with Flos and are wiped out in the destruction.
The planet's venomous insects survive the catastrophe.
There is a place called the Golden Planet.
There is an Empire significant enough to be a target of planned aggression.
Crow is a named entity capable of controlling or directing the ship's speed.
plot_events: A garden planet is annihilated in a fraction of a second.
Narration states that the planet's flowers and Zombras are incinerated, while venomous insects survive.
Inside a spacecraft, someone addresses Metablade and says its remains will be honored.
The group sets course for the Golden Planet.
A small child is prompted to burp.
An armored leader tells Crow that the victory is only partial because engineered treachery must now be used to provoke an attack on the Empire.
The leader orders maximum speed, and the ship accelerates.
uncertainties: Several names and terms are hard to read with full certainty due to image quality, especially 'Zombras' and possibly 'Metablade'.
It is visually unclear whether Metablade is a person, title, or weapon; only the remains are shown.
The exact identity of the armored leader is not stated on this page.
The exact nature of Crow is uncertain beyond being a brain-like being or interface.
visual_summary: A starship fires or streaks away through space as narration states that a garden planet is destroyed almost instantly. A second narration panel shows scorched insect-like survivors amid the devastation. Inside the ship, a figure mourns or honors the remains of a fallen blade-like weapon or person named Metablade, while others urge the ship onward to the Golden Planet. A baby is prompted to burp. A stern armored man speaks to a floating brain-like being called Crow, saying his victory is incomplete until engineered enemies attack the Empire and are dead. The ship then accelerates away at maximum speed.
